rules.rule_name: File Operation Routing
rules.rule_description: Routes the file operation request to the correct file handler based on the file identifier provided by the caller. If an unrecognized file identifier is provided, the program exits without performing any operation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
1: File Operation Routing
Which file to operate on?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program receives a file identifier (LK-M03B-DD) from the calling program
acceptance_criteria.When: The file identifier is evaluated against known file names: TRNXFILE, XREFFILE, CUSTFILE, or ACCTFILE
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the file identifier is TRNXFILE, route to Transaction File processing; if XREFFILE, route to Cross-Reference File processing; if CUSTFILE, route to Customer File processing; if ACCTFILE, route to Account File processing; if the file identifier does not match any known file name, exit the program immediately without performing any file operation

rules.rule_name: Transaction File Open
rules.rule_description: Opens the Transaction File to allow sequential reading of transaction records.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
2: Transaction File Open
Open TRNX-FILE for reading

acceptance_criteria.Given: The file identifier is TRNXFILE and the requested operation is Open
acceptance_criteria.When: The open operation is requested for the Transaction File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction File is opened for reading, and the result of the open operation is returned to the calling program

rules.rule_name: Transaction File Sequential Read
rules.rule_description: Reads the next available transaction record sequentially from the Transaction File and returns the record data to the caller.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
3: Transaction File Sequential Read
Read next transaction record

acceptance_criteria.Given: The file identifier is TRNXFILE, the Transaction File is open, and the requested operation is Read
acceptance_criteria.When: A sequential read operation is performed on the Transaction File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The next transaction record is retrieved in sequence and returned to the calling program as record data; the result of the read operation (including end-of-file condition) is returned to the calling program

rules.rule_name: Transaction File Close
rules.rule_description: Closes the Transaction File after all required transaction records have been processed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
4: Transaction File Close
Close TRNX-FILE

acceptance_criteria.Given: The file identifier is TRNXFILE and the requested operation is Close
acceptance_criteria.When: The close operation is requested for the Transaction File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction File is closed and the result of the close operation is returned to the calling program

rules.rule_name: Cross-Reference File Open
rules.rule_description: Opens the Cross-Reference File to allow sequential reading of cross-reference records.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
5: Cross-Reference File Open
Open XREF-FILE for reading

acceptance_criteria.Given: The file identifier is XREFFILE and the requested operation is Open
acceptance_criteria.When: The open operation is requested for the Cross-Reference File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Cross-Reference File is opened for reading and the result of the open operation is returned to the calling program

rules.rule_name: Cross-Reference File Sequential Read
rules.rule_description: Reads the next available record sequentially from the Cross-Reference File and returns the record data to the caller.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
6: Cross-Reference File Sequential Read
Read next cross-reference record

acceptance_criteria.Given: The file identifier is XREFFILE, the Cross-Reference File is open, and the requested operation is Read
acceptance_criteria.When: A sequential read operation is performed on the Cross-Reference File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The next cross-reference record is retrieved in sequence and returned to the calling program as record data; the result of the read operation (including end-of-file condition) is returned to the calling program

rules.rule_name: Cross-Reference File Close
rules.rule_description: Closes the Cross-Reference File after all required cross-reference records have been processed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
7: Cross-Reference File Close
Close XREF-FILE

acceptance_criteria.Given: The file identifier is XREFFILE and the requested operation is Close
acceptance_criteria.When: The close operation is requested for the Cross-Reference File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Cross-Reference File is closed and the result of the close operation is returned to the calling program

rules.rule_name: Customer File Open
rules.rule_description: Opens the Customer File to allow direct keyed retrieval of individual customer records.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
8: Customer File Open
Open CUST-FILE for random access

acceptance_criteria.Given: The file identifier is CUSTFILE and the requested operation is Open
acceptance_criteria.When: The open operation is requested for the Customer File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Customer File is opened for reading and the result of the open operation is returned to the calling program

rules.rule_name: Customer Record Lookup by Key
rules.rule_description: Retrieves a specific customer record directly from the Customer File using a Customer ID key provided by the caller. The key length is variable and specified by the caller.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
9: Customer Record Lookup by Key
Retrieve customer record by Customer ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The file identifier is CUSTFILE, the Customer File is open, the requested operation is Read by Key, and the caller has provided a Customer ID key value along with the key length
acceptance_criteria.When: A keyed read operation is performed using the provided Customer ID (trimmed to the specified key length) as the lookup key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The matching customer record is retrieved directly from the Customer File and returned to the calling program as record data; if no matching customer record is found, the not-found result is returned to the calling program

rules.rule_name: Customer File Close
rules.rule_description: Closes the Customer File after the required customer record lookup has been completed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
10: Customer File Close
Close CUST-FILE

acceptance_criteria.Given: The file identifier is CUSTFILE and the requested operation is Close
acceptance_criteria.When: The close operation is requested for the Customer File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Customer File is closed and the result of the close operation is returned to the calling program

rules.rule_name: Account File Open
rules.rule_description: Opens the Account File to allow direct keyed retrieval of individual account records.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
11: Account File Open
Open ACCT-FILE for random access

acceptance_criteria.Given: The file identifier is ACCTFILE and the requested operation is Open
acceptance_criteria.When: The open operation is requested for the Account File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Account File is opened for reading and the result of the open operation is returned to the calling program

rules.rule_name: Account Record Lookup by Key
rules.rule_description: Retrieves a specific account record directly from the Account File using an Account ID key provided by the caller. The key length is variable and specified by the caller.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:

Retrieve account record by Account ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The file identifier is ACCTFILE, the Account File is open, the requested operation is Read by Key, and the caller has provided an Account ID key value along with the key length
acceptance_criteria.When: A keyed read operation is performed using the provided Account ID (trimmed to the specified key length) as the lookup key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The matching account record is retrieved directly from the Account File and returned to the calling program as record data; if no matching account record is found, the not-found result is returned to the calling program

rules.rule_name: Account File Close
rules.rule_description: Closes the Account File after the required account record lookup has been completed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
13: Account File Close
Close ACCT-FILE

acceptance_criteria.Given: The file identifier is ACCTFILE and the requested operation is Close
acceptance_criteria.When: The close operation is requested for the Account File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Account File is closed and the result of the close operation is returned to the calling program

rules.rule_name: Operation Status Return to Caller
rules.rule_description: After every file operation (open, read, or close) on any file, the outcome of that operation is always communicated back to the calling program. This allows the caller to determine whether the operation succeeded, reached end-of-file, or failed to find a record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
14: Operation Status Return
Return operation result to caller

acceptance_criteria.Given: Any file operation (open, read, or close) has been performed on any of the four files: Transaction, Cross-Reference, Customer, or Account
acceptance_criteria.When: The file operation completes regardless of outcome
acceptance_criteria.Then: The file operation result is captured and returned to the calling program; for Transaction File operations the Transaction File result is returned; for Cross-Reference File operations the Cross-Reference File result is returned; for Customer File operations the Customer File result is returned; for Account File operations the Account File result is returned

rules.rule_name: Route File Operation Request to Appropriate File Handler
rules.rule_description: When a calling program requests a file operation, the service determines which file to operate on by evaluating the file identifier received, and routes the request to the correct file handling process for Transaction, Cross-Reference, Customer, or Account files.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Which File Identifier was Received?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A calling program has submitted a file operation request and provided a file identifier (LK-M03B-DD) indicating which file should be operated on
acceptance_criteria.When: The file operation service evaluates the received file identifier against the known file identifiers: TRNXFILE, XREFFILE, CUSTFILE, and ACCTFILE
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the identifier is 'TRNXFILE', the request is routed to the Transaction File handling process; if the identifier is 'XREFFILE', the request is routed to the Cross-Reference File handling process; if the identifier is 'CUSTFILE', the request is routed to the Customer File handling process; if the identifier is 'ACCTFILE', the request is routed to the Account File handling process; if the identifier does not match any known file identifier, no file operation is performed and the service exits immediately returning control to the calling program

rules.rule_name: Handle Unrecognized File Identifier with No Action
rules.rule_description: When the file identifier provided by the calling program does not match any of the recognized file identifiers, the service takes no action and immediately returns control to the calling program without performing any file operation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Unknown File Identifier
No Action Taken

acceptance_criteria.Given: A calling program has submitted a file operation request with a file identifier (LK-M03B-DD) that does not match any of the recognized values: TRNXFILE, XREFFILE, CUSTFILE, or ACCTFILE
acceptance_criteria.When: The file operation service evaluates the received file identifier and finds no matching known file identifier
acceptance_criteria.Then: No file operation is performed, no file is opened, read, or closed, and the service immediately exits and returns control to the calling program without updating any output data or status

rules.rule_description: When the file identifier received is TRNXFILE, the service routes the request to the Transaction File handling process to perform the requested operation on the Transaction File.

rules.rule_name: Transaction File Open Operation Eligibility Check
rules.rule_description: Determines whether the requested file operation is an OPEN request for the Transaction File. Only when the operation type is OPEN should the Transaction File be opened for sequential reading; all other operation types are not applicable to this process step.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Requested Operation = OPEN?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The file I/O service has been invoked with the Transaction File (TRNXFILE) as the target file
acceptance_criteria.When: The requested operation type is evaluated to determine if it is an OPEN request
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the operation type is OPEN, proceed to open the Transaction File for sequential reading; if the operation type is anything other than OPEN, this process step is not applicable and no action is taken

rules.rule_name: Transaction File Sequential Read Enablement
rules.rule_description: When an OPEN operation is requested for the Transaction File, the file must be opened exclusively in read (input) mode to enable sequential retrieval of transaction records. No modifications to transaction data are permitted during this operation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Open Transaction File for Sequential Reading

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction File (TRNXFILE) has been identified as the target file and the requested operation is OPEN
acceptance_criteria.When: The OPEN operation is executed on the Transaction File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction File is opened in read-only (input) mode, making it available for sequential record-by-record retrieval; no write or update access is granted

rules.rule_name: Transaction File Open Success Status Capture
rules.rule_description: Upon successfully opening the Transaction File, the resulting operation status must be captured and communicated back to the calling program to confirm that the file is available and ready for transaction record retrieval.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Capture Success Status - Ready for Transaction Record Retrieval

acceptance_criteria.Given: The OPEN operation has been executed on the Transaction File and the file has been opened successfully
acceptance_criteria.When: The Transaction File open operation completes without error
acceptance_criteria.Then: The successful operation status from the Transaction File is captured and returned to the calling program, indicating that the Transaction File is ready for sequential record retrieval

rules.rule_name: Transaction File Open Failure Status Capture
rules.rule_description: If the Transaction File cannot be opened, the failure status must be captured and communicated back to the calling program, indicating that the Transaction File is unavailable and transaction record retrieval cannot proceed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Capture Failure Status - Transaction File Unavailable

acceptance_criteria.Given: The OPEN operation has been executed on the Transaction File and the file has failed to open
acceptance_criteria.When: The Transaction File open operation completes with an error or non-success condition
acceptance_criteria.Then: The failure operation status from the Transaction File is captured and returned to the calling program, indicating that the Transaction File is unavailable and no transaction records can be retrieved

rules.rule_name: Transaction File Operation Status Return to Caller
rules.rule_description: Regardless of whether the Transaction File open operation succeeds or fails, the resulting operation status must always be returned to the calling program. This ensures the caller can determine the outcome and take appropriate next steps.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Return Operation Status to Calling Program

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction File OPEN operation has been attempted, resulting in either a success or failure status
acceptance_criteria.When: The OPEN operation processing is complete
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction File operation status (whether success or failure) is always transferred and returned to the calling program via the operation return code, enabling the caller to handle the outcome appropriately

rules.rule_name: Validate Sequential Read Operation Request for Transaction File
rules.rule_description: Determines whether the requested operation is a sequential READ before attempting to retrieve a transaction record. If the operation is not a READ, no action is taken.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Operation Request = READ?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction File I/O service has been invoked with a file identifier of 'TRNXFILE' and an operation type has been provided by the calling program
acceptance_criteria.When: The operation request is evaluated to determine if it is a sequential READ request (M03B-READ)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the operation request is a sequential READ, proceed to read the next transaction record from the Transaction File; if the operation request is any other type (Open, Close, or unrecognized), no read action is taken and processing exits without retrieving any transaction data

rules.rule_name: Read Next Transaction Record Sequentially from Transaction File
rules.rule_description: Retrieves the next available transaction record in sequential order from the Transaction File and loads the record data into the shared data area for the calling program to consume.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Read Next Transaction Record Sequentially from TRNX-FILE

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction File has been previously opened and the operation request is confirmed as a sequential READ
acceptance_criteria.When: The sequential read operation is executed against the Transaction File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The next transaction record in sequence is retrieved from the Transaction File and its full record data is placed into the shared record data field (LK-M03B-FLDT) available to the calling program

rules.rule_name: Return Transaction Record Data to Calling Program Upon Successful Retrieval
rules.rule_description: When a transaction record is successfully retrieved from the Transaction File, the complete record data is made available to the calling program through the shared data interface.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Return Transaction Record Data to Calling Program

acceptance_criteria.Given: A sequential READ operation has been executed against the Transaction File and a transaction record exists at the current file position
acceptance_criteria.When: The read operation completes successfully and a record is found
acceptance_criteria.Then: The full transaction record data is returned to the calling program via the shared record data field (LK-M03B-FLDT), and a successful operation status is returned via the status indicator (LK-M03B-RC)

rules.rule_name: Return End-of-File Indicator When No More Transaction Records Exist
rules.rule_description: When a sequential read reaches the end of the Transaction File and no further records are available, an end-of-file condition is communicated back to the calling program so it can stop requesting further records.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Return End-of-File Indicator to Calling Program

acceptance_criteria.Given: A sequential READ operation has been executed against the Transaction File and the current file position is at or beyond the last record in the file
acceptance_criteria.When: The read operation finds no more records available in the Transaction File
acceptance_criteria.Then: An end-of-file status indicator is returned to the calling program via the operation status field (LK-M03B-RC), signaling that all transaction records have been processed and no record data is populated in the shared record data field

rules.rule_name: Capture and Return Transaction File Operation Status to Calling Program
rules.rule_description: After every sequential read attempt on the Transaction File — whether successful, end-of-file, or failed — the resulting operation status is always captured and returned to the calling program to enable appropriate downstream handling.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Capture Operation Status Success / End-of-File / Failure

acceptance_criteria.Given: A sequential READ operation has been attempted on the Transaction File, resulting in one of the following outcomes: successful record retrieval, end-of-file condition, or a read failure
acceptance_criteria.When: The read operation completes regardless of outcome
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction File operation status (success, end-of-file, or failure) is captured from the file status indicator and returned to the calling program via the return code field (LK-M03B-RC), ensuring the calling program always receives the outcome of the read attempt

rules.rule_name: No Action Taken When Operation Request Is Not a Sequential Read
rules.rule_description: If the operation requested by the calling program is not a sequential READ (e.g., it is an Open or Close or unrecognized operation), the Transaction File sequential read logic is entirely bypassed and no record retrieval is attempted.

acceptance_criteria.Given: A valid Account ID key and its length have been received from the calling program
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to read from the Account File
acceptance_criteria.Then: Only the portion of the Account ID key matching the specified key length is set as the active lookup key on the Account File, ensuring the search targets the exact account record requested

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Account Record by Account ID Key
rules.rule_description: The system performs a direct keyed lookup on the Account File using the Account ID to retrieve the specific account record requested by the calling program.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Lookup by Account ID → ACCT-FILE

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account File is open for reading and the Account ID has been set as the lookup key
acceptance_criteria.When: A keyed read operation is performed on the Account File using the Account ID
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system attempts to directly locate and retrieve the account record matching the provided Account ID from the Account File

rules.rule_name: Return Account Record Data When Found
rules.rule_description: When the Account File lookup successfully locates the requested account record, the full account record data is returned to the calling program.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Return Account Record Data to Calling Program

acceptance_criteria.Given: A keyed read has been performed on the Account File using the provided Account ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The account record matching the Account ID is found in the Account File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The complete account record data is returned to the calling program, and a successful operation status is communicated back to the caller

rules.rule_name: Return Not Found Status When Account Record Does Not Exist
rules.rule_description: When the Account File lookup cannot locate a record matching the provided Account ID, a 'not found' outcome is communicated back to the calling program.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Return 'Not Found' Status to Calling Program

acceptance_criteria.Given: A keyed read has been performed on the Account File using the provided Account ID
acceptance_criteria.When: No account record matching the provided Account ID exists in the Account File
acceptance_criteria.Then: No account record data is returned, and a 'record not found' status is communicated back to the calling program so the caller can handle the absence of the account appropriately

rules.rule_name: Receive Account ID Key Field and Key Length from Calling Program
rules.rule_description: When an Account record lookup by key is requested, the program must receive both the Account ID key field value and the key length from the calling program before any key extraction or lookup can proceed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Receive Key Field containing Account ID and Key Length from calling program

acceptance_criteria.Given: A calling program has requested an Account record lookup by key and has provided a Key Field containing the Account ID value and a Key Length indicating how many characters of the Key Field represent the valid Account ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The Account File keyed read operation is triggered by the calling program
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program accepts the Key Field (containing the Account ID) and the Key Length from the calling program as the inputs required to identify the specific Account record to be retrieved

rules.rule_name: Extract Account ID from Key Field Using Specified Key Length
rules.rule_description: The Account ID must be precisely extracted from the provided Key Field by reading characters starting from position 1 up to the length specified by the Key Length value, ensuring only the valid portion of the key is used for the lookup.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Extract Account ID from Key Field using specified Key Length from position 1 to Key Length

acceptance_criteria.Given: The calling program has provided a Key Field containing the Account ID and a Key Length value specifying the number of valid characters in the Key Field
acceptance_criteria.When: The program prepares the Account ID for the file lookup
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program extracts characters from the Key Field starting at position 1 through the position indicated by the Key Length value, and this extracted substring becomes the Account ID used for the record lookup — no characters beyond the specified Key Length are included

rules.rule_name: Set Extracted Account ID as the File Lookup Key
rules.rule_description: Once the Account ID has been extracted from the Key Field using the specified Key Length, it must be set as the active lookup key on the Account File so that the correct Account record can be directly retrieved.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Extracted Account ID as the File Lookup Key

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account ID has been successfully extracted from the Key Field using the specified Key Length
acceptance_criteria.When: The program sets up the Account File for a direct keyed record retrieval
acceptance_criteria.Then: The extracted Account ID is assigned as the lookup key for the Account File, and the program proceeds to retrieve the Account record that matches this Account ID, returning the matched record data to the calling program

rules.rule_name: Variable-Length Account ID Key Supports Dynamic Key Lengths
rules.rule_description: The Account ID key extraction mechanism supports variable-length keys, meaning the calling program controls how much of the Key Field constitutes the Account ID by specifying the Key Length. This allows different callers to use different Account ID lengths without changing the lookup service.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Extract Account ID from Key Field using specified Key Length from position 1 to Key Length

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account File lookup service is designed to accept Account IDs of varying lengths
acceptance_criteria.When: A calling program provides a Key Field and a Key Length for an Account record lookup
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program uses exactly the number of characters specified by the Key Length — starting from position 1 of the Key Field — as the Account ID, ensuring the lookup is performed with the precise key boundary defined by the caller and not a fixed or default key length

rules.rule_name: Account File Close Operation Verification
rules.rule_description: Determines whether the requested operation for the Account File is a CLOSE operation before proceeding to close the file. If the operation is not CLOSE, no action is taken and the process completes without closing the file.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Operation Type = CLOSE?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account File processing service has been invoked with file identifier 'ACCTFILE' and an operation type has been provided by the calling program
acceptance_criteria.When: The operation type is evaluated to determine if it is a CLOSE request
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the operation type is CLOSE, the Account File close process is initiated; if the operation type is anything other than CLOSE, the Account File close process is skipped and the process completes without any file action

rules.rule_name: Account File Closure Execution
rules.rule_description: Closes the Account File once all required account records have been retrieved, ensuring the file is properly released after use.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Close the Account File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account File has been previously opened and the calling program has completed all required account record retrievals
acceptance_criteria.When: The operation type is confirmed as CLOSE
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Account File is closed and made unavailable for further read operations within this session

rules.rule_name: Account File Close Operation Result Capture
rules.rule_description: After the Account File close operation is executed, the outcome of the operation is captured and made available to the calling program so it can determine whether the file was successfully closed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Capture Account File Operation Result Status

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account File close operation has been executed
acceptance_criteria.When: The close operation completes — whether successfully or with an issue
acceptance_criteria.Then: The result status of the Account File close operation is captured and stored for return to the calling program

rules.rule_name: Account File Close Status Return to Caller
rules.rule_description: The outcome of the Account File close operation is always communicated back to the calling program, allowing the caller to verify whether the file was successfully closed and take appropriate action if needed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Return Operation Status to Calling Program

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account File close operation has been attempted and the operation result status has been captured
acceptance_criteria.When: The Account File close process is complete
acceptance_criteria.Then: The operation result status is returned to the calling program so the caller can confirm successful closure of the Account File or handle any closure issue accordingly

rules.rule_name: Capture and Return File Operation Result to Calling Program
rules.rule_description: After every file operation (open, read, or close) on any supported file, the outcome of that operation is captured from the respective file and communicated back to the calling program. This allows the calling program to determine whether the requested file operation succeeded or failed and take appropriate action.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Capture Transaction File Operation Result / Capture Cross-Reference File Operation Result / Capture Customer File Operation Result / Capture Account File Operation Result → Set Return Status Code for Calling Program → Return Success Status or Return Failure Status to Calling Program

acceptance_criteria.Given: A file operation (open, read, or close) has been requested and executed on one of the supported files: Transaction File, Cross-Reference File, Customer File, or Account File
acceptance_criteria.When: The file operation completes — regardless of whether it succeeded (e.g., record found, file opened successfully, end-of-file reached) or failed (e.g., record not found, file unavailable)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The operation result status from the specific file that was operated on is captured and set as the return status code passed back to the calling program: if the Transaction File was operated on, the Transaction File operation result is returned; if the Cross-Reference File was operated on, the Cross-Reference File operation result is returned; if the Customer File was operated on, the Customer File operation result is returned; if the Account File was operated on, the Account File operation result is returned — in all cases the calling program receives the status indicating success or failure of the requested operation

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program receives a file identifier (LK-M03B-DD) from the calling program
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file identifier is evaluated against known file names: TRNXFILE, XREFFILE, CUSTFILE, or ACCTFILE
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the file identifier is TRNXFILE, route to Transaction File processing; if XREFFILE, route to Cross-Reference File processing; if CUSTFILE, route to Customer File processing; if ACCTFILE, route to Account File processing; if the file identifier does not match any known file name, exit the program immediately without performing any file operation

all_rules.Rule_Name: File Operation Routing
all_rules.Rule_Description: Routes the file operation request to the correct file handler based on the file identifier provided by the caller. If an unrecognized file identifier is provided, the program exits without performing any operation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The file identifier is TRNXFILE and the requested operation is Open
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The open operation is requested for the Transaction File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction File is opened for reading, and the result of the open operation is returned to the calling program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction File Open
all_rules.Rule_Description: Opens the Transaction File to allow sequential reading of transaction records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The file identifier is TRNXFILE, the Transaction File is open, and the requested operation is Read
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A sequential read operation is performed on the Transaction File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The next transaction record is retrieved in sequence and returned to the calling program as record data; the result of the read operation (including end-of-file condition) is returned to the calling program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction File Sequential Read
all_rules.Rule_Description: Reads the next available transaction record sequentially from the Transaction File and returns the record data to the caller.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The file identifier is TRNXFILE and the requested operation is Close
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The close operation is requested for the Transaction File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction File is closed and the result of the close operation is returned to the calling program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction File Close
all_rules.Rule_Description: Closes the Transaction File after all required transaction records have been processed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The file identifier is XREFFILE and the requested operation is Open
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The open operation is requested for the Cross-Reference File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Cross-Reference File is opened for reading and the result of the open operation is returned to the calling program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Cross-Reference File Open
all_rules.Rule_Description: Opens the Cross-Reference File to allow sequential reading of cross-reference records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The file identifier is XREFFILE, the Cross-Reference File is open, and the requested operation is Read
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A sequential read operation is performed on the Cross-Reference File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The next cross-reference record is retrieved in sequence and returned to the calling program as record data; the result of the read operation (including end-of-file condition) is returned to the calling program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Cross-Reference File Sequential Read
all_rules.Rule_Description: Reads the next available record sequentially from the Cross-Reference File and returns the record data to the caller.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The file identifier is XREFFILE and the requested operation is Close
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The close operation is requested for the Cross-Reference File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Cross-Reference File is closed and the result of the close operation is returned to the calling program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Cross-Reference File Close
all_rules.Rule_Description: Closes the Cross-Reference File after all required cross-reference records have been processed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The file identifier is CUSTFILE and the requested operation is Open
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The open operation is requested for the Customer File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Customer File is opened for reading and the result of the open operation is returned to the calling program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer File Open
all_rules.Rule_Description: Opens the Customer File to allow direct keyed retrieval of individual customer records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The file identifier is CUSTFILE, the Customer File is open, the requested operation is Read by Key, and the caller has provided a Customer ID key value along with the key length
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A keyed read operation is performed using the provided Customer ID (trimmed to the specified key length) as the lookup key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The matching customer record is retrieved directly from the Customer File and returned to the calling program as record data; if no matching customer record is found, the not-found result is returned to the calling program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer Record Lookup by Key
all_rules.Rule_Description: Retrieves a specific customer record directly from the Customer File using a Customer ID key provided by the caller. The key length is variable and specified by the caller.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The file identifier is CUSTFILE and the requested operation is Close
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The close operation is requested for the Customer File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Customer File is closed and the result of the close operation is returned to the calling program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer File Close
all_rules.Rule_Description: Closes the Customer File after the required customer record lookup has been completed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The file identifier is ACCTFILE and the requested operation is Open
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The open operation is requested for the Account File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account File is opened for reading and the result of the open operation is returned to the calling program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account File Open
all_rules.Rule_Description: Opens the Account File to allow direct keyed retrieval of individual account records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The file identifier is ACCTFILE, the Account File is open, the requested operation is Read by Key, and the caller has provided an Account ID key value along with the key length
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A keyed read operation is performed using the provided Account ID (trimmed to the specified key length) as the lookup key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The matching account record is retrieved directly from the Account File and returned to the calling program as record data; if no matching account record is found, the not-found result is returned to the calling program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Record Lookup by Key
all_rules.Rule_Description: Retrieves a specific account record directly from the Account File using an Account ID key provided by the caller. The key length is variable and specified by the caller.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The file identifier is ACCTFILE and the requested operation is Close
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The close operation is requested for the Account File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account File is closed and the result of the close operation is returned to the calling program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account File Close
all_rules.Rule_Description: Closes the Account File after the required account record lookup has been completed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Any file operation (open, read, or close) has been performed on any of the four files: Transaction, Cross-Reference, Customer, or Account
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file operation completes regardless of outcome
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The file operation result is captured and returned to the calling program; for Transaction File operations the Transaction File result is returned; for Cross-Reference File operations the Cross-Reference File result is returned; for Customer File operations the Customer File result is returned; for Account File operations the Account File result is returned

all_rules.Rule_Name: Operation Status Return to Caller
all_rules.Rule_Description: After every file operation (open, read, or close) on any file, the outcome of that operation is always communicated back to the calling program. This allows the caller to determine whether the operation succeeded, reached end-of-file, or failed to find a record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A calling program has submitted a file operation request and provided a file identifier (LK-M03B-DD) indicating which file should be operated on
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file operation service evaluates the received file identifier against the known file identifiers: TRNXFILE, XREFFILE, CUSTFILE, and ACCTFILE
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the identifier is 'TRNXFILE', the request is routed to the Transaction File handling process; if the identifier is 'XREFFILE', the request is routed to the Cross-Reference File handling process; if the identifier is 'CUSTFILE', the request is routed to the Customer File handling process; if the identifier is 'ACCTFILE', the request is routed to the Account File handling process; if the identifier does not match any known file identifier, no file operation is performed and the service exits immediately returning control to the calling program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Route File Operation Request to Appropriate File Handler
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a calling program requests a file operation, the service determines which file to operate on by evaluating the file identifier received, and routes the request to the correct file handling process for Transaction, Cross-Reference, Customer, or Account files.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A calling program has submitted a file operation request with a file identifier (LK-M03B-DD) that does not match any of the recognized values: TRNXFILE, XREFFILE, CUSTFILE, or ACCTFILE
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file operation service evaluates the received file identifier and finds no matching known file identifier
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: No file operation is performed, no file is opened, read, or closed, and the service immediately exits and returns control to the calling program without updating any output data or status

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Unrecognized File Identifier with No Action
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the file identifier provided by the calling program does not match any of the recognized file identifiers, the service takes no action and immediately returns control to the calling program without performing any file operation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A calling program has submitted a file operation request and the file identifier (LK-M03B-DD) provided is 'TRNXFILE'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file operation service evaluates the file identifier and matches it to 'TRNXFILE'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The service routes the request to the Transaction File handling process, which will perform the requested operation (open, sequential read, or close) on the Transaction File and return the operation outcome to the calling program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Route to Transaction File Handling Process
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the file identifier received is TRNXFILE, the service routes the request to the Transaction File handling process to perform the requested operation on the Transaction File.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A calling program has submitted a file operation request and the file identifier (LK-M03B-DD) provided is 'XREFFILE'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file operation service evaluates the file identifier and matches it to 'XREFFILE'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The service routes the request to the Cross-Reference File handling process, which will perform the requested operation (open, sequential read, or close) on the Cross-Reference File and return the operation outcome to the calling program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Route to Cross-Reference File Handling Process
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the file identifier received is XREFFILE, the service routes the request to the Cross-Reference File handling process to perform the requested operation on the Cross-Reference File.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A calling program has submitted a file operation request and the file identifier (LK-M03B-DD) provided is 'CUSTFILE'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file operation service evaluates the file identifier and matches it to 'CUSTFILE'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The service routes the request to the Customer File handling process, which will perform the requested operation (open, keyed read by Customer ID, or close) on the Customer File and return the operation outcome to the calling program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Route to Customer File Handling Process
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the file identifier received is CUSTFILE, the service routes the request to the Customer File handling process to perform the requested operation on the Customer File.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A calling program has submitted a file operation request and the file identifier (LK-M03B-DD) provided is 'ACCTFILE'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file operation service evaluates the file identifier and matches it to 'ACCTFILE'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The service routes the request to the Account File handling process, which will perform the requested operation (open, keyed read by Account ID, or close) on the Account File and return the operation outcome to the calling program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Route to Account File Handling Process
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the file identifier received is ACCTFILE, the service routes the request to the Account File handling process to perform the requested operation on the Account File.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The file I/O service has been invoked with the Transaction File (TRNXFILE) as the target file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The requested operation type is evaluated to determine if it is an OPEN request
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the operation type is OPEN, proceed to open the Transaction File for sequential reading; if the operation type is anything other than OPEN, this process step is not applicable and no action is taken

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction File Open Operation Eligibility Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: Determines whether the requested file operation is an OPEN request for the Transaction File. Only when the operation type is OPEN should the Transaction File be opened for sequential reading; all other operation types are not applicable to this process step.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction File (TRNXFILE) has been identified as the target file and the requested operation is OPEN
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The OPEN operation is executed on the Transaction File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction File is opened in read-only (input) mode, making it available for sequential record-by-record retrieval; no write or update access is granted

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction File Sequential Read Enablement
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an OPEN operation is requested for the Transaction File, the file must be opened exclusively in read (input) mode to enable sequential retrieval of transaction records. No modifications to transaction data are permitted during this operation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The OPEN operation has been executed on the Transaction File and the file has been opened successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Transaction File open operation completes without error
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The successful operation status from the Transaction File is captured and returned to the calling program, indicating that the Transaction File is ready for sequential record retrieval

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction File Open Success Status Capture
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon successfully opening the Transaction File, the resulting operation status must be captured and communicated back to the calling program to confirm that the file is available and ready for transaction record retrieval.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The OPEN operation has been executed on the Transaction File and the file has failed to open
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Transaction File open operation completes with an error or non-success condition
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The failure operation status from the Transaction File is captured and returned to the calling program, indicating that the Transaction File is unavailable and no transaction records can be retrieved

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction File Open Failure Status Capture
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the Transaction File cannot be opened, the failure status must be captured and communicated back to the calling program, indicating that the Transaction File is unavailable and transaction record retrieval cannot proceed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction File OPEN operation has been attempted, resulting in either a success or failure status
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The OPEN operation processing is complete
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction File operation status (whether success or failure) is always transferred and returned to the calling program via the operation return code, enabling the caller to handle the outcome appropriately

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction File Operation Status Return to Caller
all_rules.Rule_Description: Regardless of whether the Transaction File open operation succeeds or fails, the resulting operation status must always be returned to the calling program. This ensures the caller can determine the outcome and take appropriate next steps.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction File I/O service has been invoked with a file identifier of 'TRNXFILE' and an operation type has been provided by the calling program
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The operation request is evaluated to determine if it is a sequential READ request (M03B-READ)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the operation request is a sequential READ, proceed to read the next transaction record from the Transaction File; if the operation request is any other type (Open, Close, or unrecognized), no read action is taken and processing exits without retrieving any transaction data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Sequential Read Operation Request for Transaction File
all_rules.Rule_Description: Determines whether the requested operation is a sequential READ before attempting to retrieve a transaction record. If the operation is not a READ, no action is taken.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction File has been previously opened and the operation request is confirmed as a sequential READ
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The sequential read operation is executed against the Transaction File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The next transaction record in sequence is retrieved from the Transaction File and its full record data is placed into the shared record data field (LK-M03B-FLDT) available to the calling program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Read Next Transaction Record Sequentially from Transaction File
all_rules.Rule_Description: Retrieves the next available transaction record in sequential order from the Transaction File and loads the record data into the shared data area for the calling program to consume.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A sequential READ operation has been executed against the Transaction File and a transaction record exists at the current file position
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The read operation completes successfully and a record is found
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The full transaction record data is returned to the calling program via the shared record data field (LK-M03B-FLDT), and a successful operation status is returned via the status indicator (LK-M03B-RC)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return Transaction Record Data to Calling Program Upon Successful Retrieval
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a transaction record is successfully retrieved from the Transaction File, the complete record data is made available to the calling program through the shared data interface.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A sequential READ operation has been executed against the Transaction File and the current file position is at or beyond the last record in the file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The read operation finds no more records available in the Transaction File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: An end-of-file status indicator is returned to the calling program via the operation status field (LK-M03B-RC), signaling that all transaction records have been processed and no record data is populated in the shared record data field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return End-of-File Indicator When No More Transaction Records Exist
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a sequential read reaches the end of the Transaction File and no further records are available, an end-of-file condition is communicated back to the calling program so it can stop requesting further records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A sequential READ operation has been attempted on the Transaction File, resulting in one of the following outcomes: successful record retrieval, end-of-file condition, or a read failure
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The read operation completes regardless of outcome
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction File operation status (success, end-of-file, or failure) is captured from the file status indicator and returned to the calling program via the return code field (LK-M03B-RC), ensuring the calling program always receives the outcome of the read attempt

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture and Return Transaction File Operation Status to Calling Program
all_rules.Rule_Description: After every sequential read attempt on the Transaction File — whether successful, end-of-file, or failed — the resulting operation status is always captured and returned to the calling program to enable appropriate downstream handling.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction File I/O service has been invoked with a file identifier of 'TRNXFILE'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The operation request is evaluated and determined to be something other than a sequential READ (M03B-READ is not set)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: No transaction record read is attempted, no record data is returned, and processing exits the sequential read section without performing any data retrieval action

all_rules.Rule_Name: No Action Taken When Operation Request Is Not a Sequential Read
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the operation requested by the calling program is not a sequential READ (e.g., it is an Open or Close or unrecognized operation), the Transaction File sequential read logic is entirely bypassed and no record retrieval is attempted.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A request has been received to process the Transaction File (TRNXFILE) and an operation type has been provided by the calling program
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The operation type is evaluated to determine if it is a CLOSE request

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Close Operation Before Closing Transaction File
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system must verify that the requested operation is a CLOSE before attempting to close the Transaction File. If the operation is not a CLOSE request, no action is taken on the Transaction File.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction File (TRNXFILE) has been previously opened and transaction records have been processed, and the calling program has submitted a CLOSE operation request

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close Transaction File Upon Valid Close Request
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a valid CLOSE operation is requested for the Transaction File, the system must close the Transaction File to release it and signal completion of all transaction record processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction File close operation has been executed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture and Return Transaction File Close Operation Outcome

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The calling program has requested an operation on the Cross-Reference File by passing the file identifier 'XREFFILE'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The operation type requested is evaluated

all_rules.Rule_Name: Cross-Reference File Open Request Routing

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The calling program has requested an OPEN operation on the Cross-Reference File identified as 'XREFFILE'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The OPEN operation is executed on the Cross-Reference File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Cross-Reference File is opened in read-only (INPUT) mode, making it available for sequential record retrieval; no write or update access is granted

all_rules.Rule_Name: Cross-Reference File Opening for Sequential Reading
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an OPEN operation is requested for the Cross-Reference File, the file is opened exclusively for sequential reading to enable card-to-account cross-reference lookups. The file is not opened for update or write operations.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An OPEN operation has been attempted on the Cross-Reference File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The open operation completes — either successfully making the file ready for sequential lookups, or unsuccessfully due to the file being unavailable
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The resulting operation status (success indicating the file is ready for sequential lookups, or failure indicating the file is unavailable) is captured and returned to the calling program via the operation return code, so the caller can take appropriate action

all_rules.Rule_Name: Cross-Reference File Open Success or Failure Status Capture
all_rules.Rule_Description: After attempting to open the Cross-Reference File, the outcome of the open operation — whether successful or unsuccessful — is captured and communicated back to the calling program so it can determine whether the file is available for subsequent cross-reference lookups.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Any operation (OPEN, READ, or CLOSE) has been attempted or evaluated on the Cross-Reference File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The operation processing completes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Cross-Reference File operation status is always moved to the return code field and passed back to the calling program, enabling the caller to determine the outcome and handle it appropriately

all_rules.Rule_Name: Cross-Reference File Operation Status Return to Caller
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon completion of any Cross-Reference File operation (including OPEN), the status of that operation is always communicated back to the calling program, regardless of whether the operation succeeded or failed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Cross-Reference file is open and a sequential read operation has been requested by the calling program
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the next cross-reference record sequentially from the Cross-Reference file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The card number and associated reference data from the next cross-reference record are loaded into the return data area available to the calling program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Sequential Read of Next Cross-Reference Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a sequential read operation is requested on the Cross-Reference file, the system retrieves the next available cross-reference record in file order and loads the card number and associated reference data into the return area for the calling program.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A sequential read operation has been performed on the Cross-Reference file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A cross-reference record is successfully found and retrieved from the file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The cross-reference record data, including the card number and all associated reference data, is loaded into the return data area for the calling program to consume

all_rules.Rule_Name: Cross-Reference Record Successfully Retrieved
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a sequential read of the Cross-Reference file successfully retrieves a record, the card number and associated reference data are made available to the calling program.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A sequential read operation has been performed on the Cross-Reference file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: No further cross-reference records are available because the end of the file has been reached
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: An end-of-file indicator is set and communicated back to the calling program, signaling that there are no more cross-reference records available for processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: End-of-File Reached on Cross-Reference File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a sequential read of the Cross-Reference file finds no more records, an end-of-file condition is signaled to the calling program indicating that all cross-reference records have been processed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A sequential read operation has been performed on the Cross-Reference file, resulting in either a successful record retrieval or an end-of-file condition
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The read operation completes regardless of whether a record was found or the end of file was reached
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The operation outcome status is returned to the calling program, enabling the caller to determine whether to continue processing more records or stop because no more cross-reference records are available

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return Cross-Reference Read Operation Status to Calling Program
all_rules.Rule_Description: After every sequential read attempt on the Cross-Reference file — whether a record was found or end-of-file was reached — the outcome status of the operation is always returned to the calling program so it can determine the next course of action.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Cross-Reference File processing service has been invoked with XREFFILE as the target file identifier
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The requested operation type is evaluated to determine if it is a CLOSE request
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the operation is a CLOSE request, the Cross-Reference File close process proceeds; if the operation is NOT a CLOSE request, no action is taken and the process exits immediately without closing the file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Close Operation Before Closing Cross-Reference File
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before closing the Cross-Reference File, the system must verify that the requested operation is specifically a CLOSE request. If it is not a CLOSE request, no action is taken and the process exits immediately without affecting the file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Cross-Reference File is currently open and has been used for cross-reference record lookups or sequential reads
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A CLOSE operation request is confirmed for the Cross-Reference File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Cross-Reference File is closed and made unavailable for further read operations in the current processing session

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close Cross-Reference File Upon Valid Close Request
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a valid CLOSE request is received for the Cross-Reference File, the system must close the Cross-Reference File to release it after all required cross-reference records have been processed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Cross-Reference File close operation has been executed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The close operation completes — whether successfully or with an issue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The resulting Cross-Reference File operation status is captured and returned to the calling program as the operation result, allowing the caller to assess the outcome of the close request

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture and Return Cross-Reference File Close Operation Outcome
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the Cross-Reference File close operation is executed, the outcome of the close operation must be captured and communicated back to the calling program so that the caller can determine whether the file was successfully closed or if an issue occurred.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A request has been received to process the Customer File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The operation type is evaluated to determine if it is an OPEN request
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the operation type is OPEN, proceed to open the Customer File for read-only access; if the operation type is anything other than OPEN, bypass the open process and end the Customer File open procedure without performing any action

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer File Open Operation Routing
all_rules.Rule_Description: Determines whether the requested operation on the Customer File is an Open request, and routes processing accordingly. If the operation is not an Open request, the Customer File open process is bypassed entirely.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A request has been received to process the Customer File and the operation type is OPEN
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Customer File open operation is executed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Customer File must be opened in read-only (Input) mode only, making it available for direct customer record lookups by Customer ID; no write or update access is granted

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer File Opened for Read-Only Access
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an Open operation is requested for the Customer File, the file is opened exclusively in read-only (Input) mode to enable subsequent customer record lookups by Customer ID. No modifications to customer data are permitted through this operation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer File open operation has been executed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Customer File is opened successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Customer File is ready to accept and process customer record lookup requests using Customer ID as the search key

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer File Open Success — File Ready for Lookups
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon successfully opening the Customer File, the file becomes available for customer record retrieval operations using Customer ID as the lookup key.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer File open operation has been executed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Customer File fails to open successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Customer File open failure is recorded, the file is not available for customer record lookups, and the failure outcome is returned to the calling program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer File Open Failure — Operation Unsuccessful
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the Customer File cannot be opened, the failure condition is captured and the outcome is communicated back to the calling program, preventing any subsequent customer record lookup attempts on an unavailable file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer File open operation has been attempted, resulting in either a success or failure outcome
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Customer File open process completes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The operation outcome status must always be captured and returned to the calling program regardless of whether the open succeeded or failed, so the caller can handle the result appropriately

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer File Operation Status Returned to Caller
all_rules.Rule_Description: After every Customer File open operation — whether successful or failed — the outcome status of the operation is always captured and returned to the calling program, enabling the caller to determine the result and take appropriate next steps.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The calling program has requested a customer record lookup and has provided a Customer ID key value and the length of that key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The customer record lookup operation is initiated with file identifier 'CUSTFILE' and a keyed-read operation type
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Customer ID key value (trimmed to the specified key length) is accepted and prepared for use as the lookup identifier against the Customer File

all_rules.Rule_Name: Receive Customer ID Key from Calling Program
all_rules.Rule_Description: The customer record lookup service accepts a Customer ID key and its length from the calling program to identify which customer record to retrieve.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Customer ID key value and its length have been received from the calling program
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to look up the customer record in the Customer File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Only the relevant portion of the Customer ID key — from position 1 up to the specified key length — is set as the active lookup key for the Customer File

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Customer ID as File Lookup Key
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Customer ID provided by the calling program is assigned as the active search key for the Customer File, using only the portion of the key up to the specified key length.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer ID has been set as the active lookup key for the Customer File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A keyed read operation is executed against the Customer File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system attempts to directly locate and retrieve the customer record that matches the provided Customer ID from the Customer File

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Customer Record from Customer File by Key
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system performs a direct keyed lookup against the Customer File using the Customer ID to retrieve the matching customer record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A keyed read operation has been executed against the Customer File using the provided Customer ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Customer File contains a record matching the provided Customer ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return Customer Record Data to Calling Program on Successful Lookup
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a customer record matching the provided Customer ID is found in the Customer File, the full customer record data is returned to the calling program.

Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A 'record not found' status is returned to the calling program, indicating that no customer record was located for the given Customer ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return Not Found Status When Customer Record Does Not Exist
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no customer record matching the provided Customer ID exists in the Customer File, a 'not found' outcome is communicated back to the calling program.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Customer File Close request has been received with file identifier set to 'CUSTFILE'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Verify Close Operation Type Before Closing Customer File

Acceptance_Criteria.When: The CLOSE operation is executed on the Customer File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Customer File is closed and released, making it no longer accessible for read operations until it is reopened

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close Customer File Upon Valid Close Request

Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Customer File operation status (CUSTFILE-STATUS) is moved into the return code field (LK-M03B-RC) and made available to the calling program, indicating whether the close was successful or encountered an issue

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture and Return Customer File Close Operation Outcome
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the Customer File close operation is performed, the system must capture the outcome of the close operation and return it to the calling program so the caller can determine whether the Customer File was successfully closed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The calling program has submitted a request targeting the Account File (LK-M03B-DD = 'ACCTFILE')

all_rules.Rule_Name: Route to Account File Open Operation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Determines whether the requested operation for the Account File is an Open request, and routes accordingly to either initiate the file open process or bypass it for a different operation type.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Account File for Random Access Reading

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return Account File Open Status to Calling Program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Receive Account ID Key from Calling Program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Account ID as Lookup Key

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Account Record by Account ID Key

description:
CBSTM03B is a batch COBOL subroutine (called program) that serves as a file I/O handler for the CardDemo Transaction Report application. It provides open, close, sequential read, and keyed read operations on four indexed VSAM files — Transaction, Cross-Reference, Customer, and Account — on behalf of a calling driver program. The calling program passes a data area specifying the target file, the operation to perform, an optional key, and a data buffer, and this subroutine returns the file status code after each operation.
- **Execution Environment**: Batch - **Database Access**: VSAM (Indexed Files) - **MQ Calls**: No - **Module Type**: Called module
### Key Functionalities: 1: File Operation Routing - Determine which file to operate on (Transaction, Cross-Reference, Customer, or Account) based on the file identifier passed by the calling program, and route to the appropriate file handling process 2: Transaction File Open - Open the Transaction file for sequential reading to enable subsequent transaction record retrieval 3: Transaction File Sequential Read - Read the next transaction record sequentially from the Transaction file and return the record data to the calling program 4: Transaction File Close - Close the Transaction file after all required transaction records have been processed 5: Cross-Reference File Open - Open the Card Cross-Reference file for sequential reading to enable card-to-account cross-reference lookups 6: Cross-Reference File Sequential Read - Read the next cross-reference record sequentially from the Cross-Reference file and return the record data (card number and associated reference data) to the calling program 7: Cross-Reference File Close - Close the Cross-Reference file after all required cross-reference records have been processed 8: Customer File Open - Open the Customer file for random access reading to enable customer record lookups by customer ID 9: Customer Record Lookup by Key - Retrieve a specific customer record from the Customer file using the customer ID key provided by the calling program, and return the customer data 10: Customer File Close - Close the Customer file after all required customer records have been retrieved 11: Account File Open - Open the Account file for random access reading to enable account record lookups by account ID 12: Account Record Lookup by Key - Retrieve a specific account record from the Account file using the account ID key provided by the calling program, and return the account data 13: Account File Close - Close the Account file after all required account records have been retrieved 14: Operation Status Return - Return the file operation result/status code back to the calling program after each file operation to indicate success or failure of the requested operation
